activities.anchor: Steve Blank's definition is the load-bearing sentence
activities.caption: one line of the definition's consequences is wrong
activities.name: evDefSpot

config.prompt: One line of this summary of Blank's definition is wrong. Find it.
lines: A startup is a temporary organisation, not a small version of a large company
It is searching for a repeatable, scalable business model
The search runs under extreme uncertainty
Because the model is unknown, the right tools are detailed five-year plans
The cap table and the funding ladder exist to buy time for the search
config.correction: Because the model is unknown, the right tools are experiments — the search cannot be planned, only tested.
config.why: Searching is an experimental activity: plans execute known models, experiments find unknown ones. Under extreme uncertainty the method must also be cheap, because the base rates are brutal.

activities.anchor: Most new businesses are sole traders or partnerships for a reason
activities.caption: run the incorporation decision
activities.name: evFormBranch

config.root: You are incorporation-shopping for a new venture. Every choice has consequences — pick a path.

start.text: You need to form quickly, keep total control, and no outside equity is needed yet. What do you become?

choices.label: Sole trader
choices.feedback: Formation instant, control total, profits face no double layer — and unlimited liability is yours.

choices.label: Private limited company (Ltd / LLC / C-corp)
choices.feedback: Safe but heavier: this is the form for selling shares, which you do not need yet.

choices.label: Public listed company
choices.feedback: Far beyond the startup stage — the ladder's top rung, not its first.

sole.text: Two years on, you are raising outside equity. What has to change?

choices.label: Convert to a private limited company and sell shares
choices.feedback: Exactly — selling shares is the precondition for outside equity investment, and dilution becomes possible.

choices.label: Stay a sole trader and borrow the money
choices.feedback: Venture debt buys runway without dilution but must be repaid regardless of success.

ltd.text: The investor asks for a stake. What are you selling?

choices.label: Shares — equity for a return
choices.feedback: The cap table exists now: every round sells equity and dilutes.

choices.label: A loan to be repaid
choices.feedback: That is venture debt, not a funding round — no dilution, but repayment regardless of success.

plc.text: A public listing is far beyond the startup stage — come back down the ladder and form something small first.

convert.text: The corporate form is in place: the funding ladder from pre-seed to series A can now run.

debt.text: Runway bought, ownership kept — at the price of repayment whatever happens.

config.why: Every funding round in this lesson presumes the corporate form that makes dilution possible — formation choices are strategy, not bureaucracy.

activities.caption: pair each stakeholder with what they want
activities.name: evStakeMatch

config.prompt: One firm, four objectives — pair each stakeholder with theirs:

pairs.right: control and wealth — which pull apart

config.why: Survival dominates the first years, and good founders name these trade-offs early instead of discovering them in a dispute.

activities.caption: run one cycle of the lean loop
activities.name: evLeanOrder

config.prompt: One cycle of the lean loop, in order:
items: Frame one measurable hypothesis — 'do 5% of visitors pre-order?'
Build the smallest artefact that generates real behaviour — the MVP
Put it in front of real users
Measure what they do, not what they say
Accept the result — even when six months of work say otherwise
config.why: The unit of progress is validated learning; the point of an MVP is to be wrong cheaply, because every feature is an expensive bet.

activities.caption: stack the sources ladder, cheapest first
activities.name: evLadderOrder

config.prompt: The sources ladder — order it, cheapest capital first:
items: Personal savings and revenue — customer money dilutes nothing
Friends and family — fast, warm, socially risky
Angel investors — tens to hundreds of thousands, for a prototype with early users
Seed funds, then venture capital series A and beyond
config.why: The ladder matches money to proof. Venture debt sits apart — runway without dilution, repaid regardless of success — and bootstrapping on revenue preserves 100% of the equity.

activities.caption: which curve is the founder's stake?
activities.name: evDilutionTrace

config.prompt: Each round dilutes everyone by 20%. Which curve shows the founder's stake across rounds?
config.why: 40 → 32 → 25.6 → 20.5: three such rounds leave 20.5%. Model the cap table three rounds forward before signing round one — and remember the option pool, often created post-money, dilutes the founders.

activities.anchor: A term sheet prices the round and sets the rights
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the clauses that matter
activities.name: evTermsCloze

config.text: The document prices the round and sets the rights: the clause that matters most is the %%0%% %%1%% — who is paid first when the company sells. Founder shares carry vesting: four years with a one-year %%2%%, protecting cofounders when someone leaves early.
config.hint: One clause decides the exit maths; the other protects cofounders from each other.

activities.anchor: A pitch deck is not a story about the product
activities.caption: file the deck's evidence by checklist
activities.name: evPitchBuckets

config.prompt: An investor's mental checklist, three boxes. File each pitch element:

items.label: total addressable market, top-down and bottom-up
the slice your current channels can reach
750,000 for 18 months of runway, tied to milestones
a bottom-up build to 72 million a year

config.why: A pitch deck is an argument about a return: evidence of engagement beats projection decks, and the ask ties the number to milestones the next round can price higher.
